title: 19th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The sitting ran from 9:06 to 11:14 on 14 May 2026. The Speaker announced committee deadlines, ruled that a journalist-detention matter could not be taken up as an urgent matter, and sent a presidential ambassador request to committee. MPs then debated the Cyber Security Bill and three committee reports (human organ transplants, the Pension Act amendment and the Decentralisation Act amendment). After a break, the House voted to extend the first session to 31 May 2026 and passed the three bills; several heated exchanges over staying on topic occurred, and one member was told to leave the chamber.

items.title: Opening of the sitting
items.outcome: opened by the Speaker with prayers

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 38 present, 6 on leave, 4 on official travel when opened (72 present by the votes)

items.title: Committee deadlines set under Rule 174: Fisheries Act amendment bill and Tax Administration Act amendment bill
Extending the first session of 2026 beyond 15 May
items.outcome: Speaker announced intent to extend to 31 May; put to vote later, passed 58-11

items.title: Urgent matter submitted by South Galolhu MP Meekail Ahmed Nasym (journalist's detention)
items.outcome: Speaker ruled it cannot be treated as an urgent matter

items.title: President's letter naming ambassadors for approval (Constitution Art. 115(d))
items.outcome: sent to the Foreign Relations Committee

items.title: Cyber Security Bill (government bill, sponsor Central Henveyru MP Hussain Nasih): continued debate
items.outcome: debated; no vote in this part

items.title: Social Committee report on the Human Organ Transplantation Bill (government bill)
Independent Institutions Committee report on the Pension Act (Law 8/2009) amendment bill
Decentralisation Committee report on the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) amendment bill
Votes
items.outcome: session extension and the three committee-report bills all passed after a 10:26 to 11:01 break

items.title: Close of sitting
items.outcome: next sitting set for Monday 18 May 2026 at 9:00

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Backed the Cyber Security Bill as a legal framework and national agency for cyber defence, after the Speaker warned another member.
Presented the Decentralisation Committee report on the Decentralisation Act amendment.
Argued atoll councils have gained powers through the changes and that LGA and Civil Service concerns were addressed.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised points of order over speaking time and the Speaker's handling of interruptions.
On the Pension amendment, questioned the 12-month terminal illness test and the MVR 5,000 income provisions.
Opposed the Decentralisation amendment, arguing councils lose income from the block grant deductions.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said cyber security matters for sovereignty but tied it to a recent virus incident at the President's Office; repeatedly told by the Speaker to stay on the bill and was later named.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Raised a point of order that a colleague's remarks were off the Pension bill.
Supported the Pension report, saying it allows pension use for housing, terminal illness and Hajj, and defended the Decentralisation changes.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: Presented the Social Committee report on the Human Organ Transplantation Bill, explaining its purpose and the committee's work after the Speaker warned another member.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Opposed the Decentralisation amendment, citing voters' rejection of constitutional changes and the removal of atoll council powers, and said councils need more funding.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the Decentralisation amendment as sound, said the atoll council structure is wasteful, and raised an unrelated condolence remark that the Speaker limited.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Opposed the Decentralisation amendment, saying the LGA would lose powers and council services and funding would suffer; also raised a point of order about the Speaker's conduct.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: As a committee member, said LGA and the Civil Service Commission raised concerns about the President-appointed chief executive having authority over staff.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the Cyber Security Bill as overdue legal protection against cyber attacks, including a national cyber security agency and critical-infrastructure standards.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported a cyber security law as services digitise, said committee stage should refine it, and argued laws set the rules courts follow.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the organ transplant bill report, citing clearer standards for transplants and benefits for the health system.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Took the floor on the organ transplant report but offered to yield, with no debate recorded.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions Committee report on the Pension Act amendment, including board size and CEO appointment changes.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the Decentralisation amendment, saying it is minor, brings LGA staff under civil service rules, and that earlier remarks were unfounded.

decisions: Committee deadlines of 30 June 2026 were announced for the Fisheries Act and Tax Administration Act amendment bills.
The Speaker ruled the journalist-detention matter could not be taken as an urgent matter under the Rules.
The President's ambassador request was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The first session of 2026 was extended to 31 May 2026 (58-11).
The Human Organ Transplantation Bill was passed (68-0).
The Pension Act amendment bill was passed (61-8-1).
The Decentralisation Act amendment bill was passed (59-10).
The next sitting was set for Monday 18 May 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Extending the first session of 2026 to 31 May 2026
Human Organ Transplantation Bill (Social Committee report)
Pension Act (Law 8/2009) amendment bill (Independent Institutions Committee report)
Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) amendment bill (Decentralisation Committee report)
